messages:
oncall-bot: Paging SRE oncall: multiple nodes in cluster 'us-west-2-inference' reporting kubelet restart loops and transient NotReady states affecting node pool 'inference-pool-prod'. Observed 15+ node flaps in last 7m. Pods in inference namespace are being rescheduled/evicted. Impact: increased 5xxs and token generation latency for some customers. Paging severity: P1. @alex.nguyen @jia.chen

alex.nguyen: acknowledged — I'm on it. Starting quick triage.

jia.chen: I'm awake, joining. Can someone dump the node list and recent kubelet logs?

alex.nguyen: grabbing node statuses now.

alex.nguyen: kubectl get nodes --selector=pool=inference-pool-prod -o wide shows several nodes cycling NotReady -> Ready. Example: ip-10-0-12-45.us-west-2.ec2.internal NotReady 5m, ip-10-0-9-33 Ready 2m, ip-10-0-7-81 NotReady 1m

alex.nguyen: main pattern: kubelet restarts every ~3-6 minutes, then node briefly Ready, then NotReady. docker/containerd shows pods get terminated; some inference containers crash with SIGSEGV around same time.

maria.santos: seeing related alerts from runtime: GPU driver lost on several nodes right before kubelet restart. Example from /var/log/syslog: 

```
Mar 15 03:44:12 ip-10-0-12-45 kernel: NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 15 03:44:12 ip-10-0-12-45 nvidia-modeset: probe: Loading probe for NVIDIA driver
Mar 15 03:44:13 systemd: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=11/SEGV
```

maria.santos: so it looks like a hardware link/GPU driver level fault causing processes to crash, kubelet then restarts.

samir.khan: that explains the SIGSEGV in containers — the inference runtime tries to attach to GPU, driver disappears, gets bad state. We should isolate the affected nodes and failover traffic.

jia.chen: agreed. Immediate mitigation recommendations: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) evict pods gracefully to fallback pool, 3) scale up a warm spare pool without GPUs to serve CPU-quantized variants, 4) temporarily route traffic to dedicated fallback model variant with lower GPU need.

alex.nguyen: executing cordon for nodes with repeated kubelet restarts.

alex.nguyen: ```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-45
kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```

oncall-bot: Automated mitigation: cordon performed on 4 nodes. Eviction started for inference deployments; autoscaler triggered +10 CPU-only pods in 'inference-fallback-cpu' pool.

pagerduty-bot: PD escalations: oncall acknowledged at 03:46 UTC. Team: SRE. Incident owner: alex.nguyen.

maria.santos: rolling a temporary kubelet config tweak: bump kubelet 'node-status-update-frequency' and 'eviction-hard' thresholds to reduce churn while we assess. Note: this reduces sensitivity to transient GPU driver resets but is a risk if nodes are truly unhealthy. Doing it on affected ASG only.

jia.chen: please paste the exact kubelet flags you set.

maria.santos: doing a daemonset patch to add args: 
```
--node-status-update-frequency=20s -> 60s
--eviction-hard=memory.available<100Mi,nodefs.available<5%
```
Applied to nodes in auto-scaling-group inference-asg-3 (rolling).

samir.khan: good. Also enabling fallback routing in the API gateway for models pinned to GPU-backed pools. Gateway rule set: route 'model:prod-*-gpu' -> 'model:prod-*-cpu-fallback' for 50% of requests from affected customers. Will ramp as we confirm stability.

alex.nguyen: customer impact quick summary: 4 customers saw spikes in 5xx rates and ~2x latency for ~8-12 minutes during flaps. Most requests retried by client and succeeded after failover. No data loss. Notifying CSMs for affected accounts now.

jia.chen: are there any signs of ECU/instance host memory leaks or OOMs?

maria.santos: the evidence points at GPU driver (NVRM) disconnects rather than OOM. Kernel logs have PCI bus resets. No consistent OOM killer entries.

samir.khan: next steps: 1) cordon + drain all nodes flapping, 2) spin new GPU nodes from a different instance type (same family but different host HW) to test if it's host-level degradation, 3) escalate to cloud provider to check hardware/network fabric, 4) prepare a rolling replacement plan for the ASG.

alex.nguyen: provisioning new nodes in a separate ASG: `inference-asg-4` with same AMI but with instance spread across different AZs. I'll bring up 6 nodes and run soak test.

oncall-bot: action item logged: ASG replacement + provider support. Ticket INF-1347 created. Assigned to: alex.nguyen, maria.santos.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: handoff in 2h. If this remains active at handoff, follow the oncall handoff protocol.

jia.chen: quick note for after-action: capture kernel oops, full dmesg, and GPU driver version across nodes; correlate with instance host IDs and AZs. That will help provider triage.

maria.santos: grabbed dmesg snippets and driver version: NVIDIA driver 515.76, CUDA 11.7. Also found one node with mixed driver version 470 leftover from a botched AMI bake — possible mismatch. Logging that to INF-1347.

alex.nguyen: rolling replacement started for nodes with mismatched driver. New nodes healthy so far. Soak test (run inference load) passing on CPU-fallback pool, GPU nodes still flapping but reduced after draining.

samir.khan: proposing a temporary traffic policy: for any model served on inference-pool-prod, enable automatic fallback to cached outputs for repeated prompts and increase prefix caching TTL from 30s -> 2m. That will reduce GPU pressure.

alex.nguyen: implemented cache TTL change in config service. Will monitor hit rate.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff: @sre-lead will take first watch if this persists past 05:30 UTC.

sre-lead: acknowledged. I'll shadow for the handoff and coordinate with cloud provider. If we see more than 10 nodes failing in an hour, escalate to infra leadership.

maria.santos: status update 04:12 UTC — drain/cordon completed on 9 nodes, new ASG nodes joining with healthy kubelet and driver. Observed CUDA driver alive on replaced hosts. No new flaps in last 7 minutes on replacement ASG.

alex.nguyen: customer impact update for internal comms: 4 customers experienced transient errors. We'll send a proactive note: brief incident summary, mitigations done, and follow-up actions (driver mismatch root cause investigation + ASG replacement). Drafting message for CSMs.

jia.chen: please include any correlation IDs or sample request IDs we can share for debugging.

alex.nguyen: adding sample request ids and timestamps to the incident ticket.

samir.khan: planning postmortem checklist: 1) root cause: confirm driver mismatch + host-level PCI resets, 2) why node flaps caused kubelet restarts rather than graceful pod handling, 3) evaluate auto-heal policies for ASG and blacklisting hosts at provisioning time if NVRM errors observed, 4) improve alerting to surface GPU driver reboots earlier.

oncall-bot: Incident severity lowered to P2 at 04:45 UTC after stabilization. Monitoring for 30m window.

sre-lead: I'll coordinate the provider ticket and follow up on replacement host batch IDs. Thanks everyone on the rapid mitigation.

alex.nguyen: handing off to @sre-lead for next watch. Leaving detailed runbook steps in INF-1347. Signing off for now.

sre-lead: taking ownership for watch window. If anything regresses ping me directly or re-open PD.

pagerduty-bot: incident acknowledged by sre-lead at 04:46 UTC.

maria.santos: one more note — we'll also add an infra check in our AMI bake to verify NVIDIA driver version alignment and fail bake if mismatched. Adding to infra backlog.

alex.nguyen: thanks team. I'll follow up on postmortem once provider returns correlation data. :thumbsup:
